score_rationale: Strong ESG/sustainability market with clear enterprise willingness-to-pay (Sustainalytics, MSCI ESG charge $5K–$50K/year). Data is a direct CSV download from EPA with no auth required. Buyer segments are professional and high-margin. Score 7 not 8 because the primary ESG buyers skew enterprise (harder first-sale path than safety consultants) and TRI data awareness among buyers is already moderate.
summary: A cleaned CSV of all US facilities reporting to the EPA Toxic Release Inventory (TRI) — publicly downloadable as a flat ZIP from EPA's TRI Data & Tools portal without authentication. Each record includes the facility name, parent company, street address, city, state, ZIP, NAICS code, chemicals reported, total release quantities by media (air, water, land, underground injection), total on-site releases, total off-site transfers, and reporting year. Sustainalytics (Morningstar), MSCI ESG, and Bloomberg Terminal's ESG module charge $5,000–$50,000+/year for ESG data that incorporates TRI chemical release records for the same ~22,000 facilities. A $49 one-time CSV targets environmental compliance attorneys prospecting for TRI-reporting clients, corporate ESG teams benchmarking peers, insurance underwriters assessing environmental liability, and sustainability consultants building environmental profiles — all of whom currently pay enterprise rates to access the identical EPA public dataset.

audience.who: Environmental compliance attorneys and law firms that represent TRI-reporting facilities in EPA enforcement proceedings, permitting, and community right-to-know litigation — every TRI reporter is a potential law firm client; corporate ESG/sustainability managers benchmarking their facility's TRI release quantities against industry peers and competitors in the same NAICS code; environmental liability insurance underwriters (Zurich, AIG Environmental) who screen facility chemical release history before writing pollution liability policies; sustainability consultants and ESG advisory firms building environmental profiles for corporate clients preparing for SEC climate disclosure; environmental justice researchers and advocacy organizations tracking chemical hotspots by zip code or census tract.

data_wanted: EPA TRI Basic Plus Data File — downloadable as a ZIP of pipe-delimited flat files from https://www.epa.gov/toxics-release-inventory-tri-program/tri-basic-plus-data-files-calendar-years-1987-present. Most recent full year: 2023 TRI data (released October 2024). Key fields per facility-chemical combination: facility name, TRI facility ID, parent company name, street address, city, county, state, ZIP, NAICS primary code, latitude/longitude, chemical name, CAS number, SIC code, total on-site releases (air fugitive, air stack, water surface, underground injection, land releases in pounds), total off-site transfers, clean air act chemical flag, PBT (persistent bioaccumulative toxic) flag, carcinogen flag, release year. Approximately 22,000 unique facilities report annually, generating ~90,000 facility-chemical records per year. Target output: single-year CSV with one row per facility (aggregated total releases across all chemicals) plus a separate chemicals-detail file.

willingness_to_pay.signal: The ESG data market is demonstrably price-insensitive at the enterprise level (Sustainalytics, MSCI charge 5-figure annual fees). The arbitrage opportunity: TRI data is free from EPA; the value-add is cleaning, normalizing, and packaging it as an importable CSV. The bottom of the market — environmental compliance attorneys, boutique ESG consultants, insurance underwriters at mid-sized carriers — cannot justify a $10K Sustainalytics subscription for one data layer but would trivially spend $49 on a clean TRI facility CSV. Environmental attorneys in particular are a high-conviction buyer: identifying the 22,000 TRI-reporting facilities in their state/NAICS specialty is worth one consultation intake call ($300–$500).
